newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore lunch shares up, no temptations on menu.
newsitem.headline: Singapore lunch shares up, no temptations on menu.

text.p: A late morning surge pushed Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index up 10 points at lunch on Thursday, but dealers said the sentiment that would keep it firmer for the rest of the day was missing.
"The buyers are just not out there," one broker at a local institution said.
With no fizz in the market, just 44 million shares changed hands in a sputtering morning session.
"Investors are taking a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the Hong Kong handover," another dealer said.
"When it's completed I think the funds will flow into Asia and Singapore will benefit," he said.
The Singapore-listed shares of Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson were up US$0.15 at US$7.75. The stock has been gaining on market rumours that it could re-list in Hong Kong.
The morning's top gainer was Malaysian over the counter traded Samanda Holdings, up Singapore $0.60 to S$11.90.
HTP Holdings was the most active share, rising two cents to S$1.13 on the strength of the showing of its related companies, including China Everbright, in Hong Kong.
